**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [CD31 (PECAM1)+Alexa Fluor 647, Lectin (凝集素)+Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based clearing method optimized for strong delipidation and high refractive index matching in dense tissues like adult mouse brain with embedded glioblastoma, enabling deep penetration of antibodies and dyes while preserving 3D vascular architecture. It is compatible with both Alexa Fluor 488 and Alexa Fluor 647, which are ideal for dual-channel imaging of vasculature. CD31 (PECAM1) is a well-established endothelial-specific marker for both normal and tumor-associated blood vessels, while fluorescently conjugated Lectin (e.g., *Lycopersicon esculentum* or *Griffonia simplicifolia* isolectin B4) provides complementary labeling of perfused and functional vasculature, including microvessels at the invasive front. This dual-labeling strategy robustly visualizes the entire vascular network—tumor core, margin, and adjacent normal parenchyma—enabling precise spatial analysis of GBM cell invasion along perivascular spaces. FDISCO’s compatibility with exogenous fluorophores (unlike iDISCO+ which quenches GFP/YFP) and minimal fluorescence loss ensures high signal-to-noise for long-term 3D imaging.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional, if endogenous pigments present)  
2.1 Incubation with 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration (for immunolabeling)  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum (NGS).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with anti-CD31 (PECAM1) primary antibody diluted 1:200 in PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100 + 5% NGS.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  

6 Wash  
6.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Repeat wash step 6.1 two more times (total 3 washes).  

7 Secondary Antibody and Lectin Co-staining  
7.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-rat (or appropriate host) secondary antibody (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated Lectin (e.g., *Lycopersicon esculentum* lectin, 10 µg/mL) in PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100 + 5% NGS.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  

8 Post-staining Wash  
8.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
8.2 Repeat wash step 8.1 two more times (total 3 washes).  

9 Dehydration (post-labeling)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation  
10.1 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Repeat step 10.2 once.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) ethyl cinnamate (ECi).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
11.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) ECi.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

12 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
12.1 Transfer sample to glass vial filled with fresh ECi and store at RT in the dark until imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite)

**Chosen Method:** MACS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP (内源), MAP2 + Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires preservation of weak endogenous fluorescent protein signals (e.g., GFP) in sparse neurons while resolving fine dendritic morphology. MACS is an aqueous-based, non-denaturing clearing method that robustly preserves endogenous GFP/YFP/tdTomato fluorescence, minimizes tissue distortion, and supports deep antibody penetration—critical for immunolabeling structural markers like MAP2 in 3 mm brain blocks. MAP2 specifically labels dendrites and soma of mature neurons, complementing sparse endogenous GFP to enhance visualization of dendritic arborization, branch points, and local projection patterns without relying solely on weak intrinsic signal. Alexa Fluor 488 is compatible with MACS and spectrally separable from GFP if needed, though often used to amplify GFP-like signal. This dual-labeling strategy ensures reliable 3D reconstruction even when endogenous fluorescence is faint.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunolabeling (post-fixation, pre-clearing)  
1.1 Wash tissue 3 × 1 hour in PBS with 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  
1.2 Incubate in blocking solution: 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.3 Incubate with primary antibody: anti-MAP2 (chicken or mouse monoclonal, 1:500 dilution) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
1.4 Wash thoroughly: 5 × 2 hours in PBST. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours per wash)  
1.5 Incubate with secondary antibody: Alexa Fluor 488–conjugated anti-host IgG (1:800 dilution) in blocking solution, protected from light. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
1.6 Wash thoroughly: 5 × 2 hours in PBST, then 2 × 1 hour in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: as indicated)  

2 Tissue Optical Clearing  
2.1 Incubation with MACS-R0 (20 vol% N-methylnicotinamide (MXDA), 15% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.40). (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with MACS-R1 (40 vol% MXDA, 30% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.48). (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with MACS-R2 (40 vol% MXDA, 50% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.51). (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Refractive Index Matching and Storage  
3.1 Transfer cleared tissue into fresh MACS-R2 for long-term storage at 4 ℃ in the dark. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: indefinite)  
3.2 Prior to imaging, equilibrate sample in fresh MACS-R2 for at least 2 hours at RT to ensure optical homogeneity. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

**Chosen Method:** MACS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP (内源), MAP2 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** The sample contains weak endogenous GFP signal in sparse reporter neurons and requires long-term preservation of fluorescence for repeat imaging after ~6 months. MACS is an aqueous, non-denaturing clearing method that preserves endogenous fluorescent proteins (including GFP) with minimal quenching, supports deep antibody penetration in 3 mm brain blocks, and causes negligible tissue distortion—critical for accurate morphometric analysis of dendritic arborization. MAP2 is a well-established pan-dendritic marker that complements sparse GFP-labeled neurons by revealing the full dendritic skeleton, enabling robust quantification of branch complexity and local circuit architecture. Alexa Fluor 647 is highly photostable and compatible with MACS, ensuring signal integrity during long-term storage and repeated imaging sessions.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunolabeling (post-fixation, pre-clearing)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution: 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibody: anti-MAP2 (e.g., mouse monoclonal, 1:500) in blocking solution (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
1.3 Wash with PBST (0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS): 3 × 1 hour each (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibody: donkey anti-mouse IgG conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) in blocking solution (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
1.5 Wash with PBST: 3 × 1 hour each (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

2 Tissue Optical Clearing  
2.1 Incubation with MACS-R0 (20 vol% MXDA, 15% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.40) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with MACS-R1 (40 vol% MXDA, 30% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.48) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with MACS-R2 (40 vol% MXDA, 50% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.51) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Refractive Index Matching and Long-Term Storage  
3.1 Transfer samples into fresh MACS-R2 in light-protected glass vials with tight-sealing caps (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: indefinite)  
3.2 Store at 4 ℃ in the dark for up to 6 months; prior to imaging, equilibrate at RT for 1 hour in fresh MACS-R2 to minimize thermal drift during acquisition.

**Chosen Method:** MACS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP (内源), MAP2 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** The problem requires preservation of weak endogenous fluorescent protein signals (e.g., GFP/YFP) in 3 mm mouse brain blocks, compatibility with long-term storage (~6 months), and high-fidelity visualization of sparse neuronal morphology—including fine dendritic arbors. MACS is an aqueous-based clearing method that preserves endogenous fluorescence (including GFP), enables deep antibody penetration into thick tissue, minimizes tissue distortion, and uses low-toxicity reagents suitable for archival storage. Among structural markers, MAP2 is a well-established dendrite-specific cytoskeletal protein that complements sparse endogenous GFP-labeled neurons by revealing full dendritic architecture without labeling non-target cells. Alexa Fluor 647 is highly photostable, compatible with MACS, and spectrally separable from GFP, enabling dual-channel 3D reconstruction. This combination meets all requirements: FP preservation, dendritic detail, minimal shrinkage, and long-term signal stability.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunolabeling (post-fixation, pre-clearing)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution: 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum, 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibody: anti-MAP2 (mouse or rabbit monoclonal, 1:500 dilution) in blocking solution (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours with gentle agitation)  
1.3 Washing: 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS, 3 changes (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibody: Alexa Fluor 647–conjugated anti-host IgG (1:800 dilution) in blocking solution (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours with gentle agitation)  
1.5 Washing: 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS, 3 changes (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

2 Tissue Optical Clearing  
2.1 Incubation with MACS-R0 (20 vol% N-methylnicotinamide [MXDA], 15% w/v sorbitol in PBS, pH 7.4) (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with MACS-R1 (40 vol% MXDA, 30% w/v sorbitol in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with MACS-R2 (40 vol% MXDA, 50% w/v sorbitol in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Refractive Index Matching and Storage  
3.1 Transfer tissue to final RI-matching solution: MACS-R3 (50 vol% MXDA, 60% w/v sorbitol in PBS, RI ≈ 1.52) (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  
3.2 Store samples long-term in MACS-R3 at 4 ℃ in the dark in sealed glass vials (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: up to 6 months)  

4 Imaging Preparation (prior to microscopy)  
4.1 Equilibrate sample in fresh MACS-R3 at RT for 2 hours before imaging to ensure optical homogeneity (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Lectin (凝集素)+Alexa Fluor 647, Claudin-5+Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based clearing method optimized for adult mouse brain and tumor tissue up to ~10 mm, offering strong delipidation power, deep antibody/dye penetration, and excellent preservation of exogenous fluorophores like Alexa Fluor dyes. It is compatible with both Lectin (for pan-endothelial labeling of functional vasculature) and Claudin-5 (a tight junction protein critical for blood–brain barrier integrity), enabling simultaneous 3D visualization of vascular architecture and barrier continuity. Unlike aqueous methods (e.g., CUBIC, ScaleS), FDISCO achieves faster and more complete clearing in dense GBM tissue while minimizing light scattering. The use of Alexa Fluor 647 (far-red) and Alexa Fluor 488 (green) ensures spectral separation and high signal stability during dehydration and refractive index matching.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional for endogenous pigment reduction)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration (for immunolabeling)  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 10% (vol/vol) DMSO + 6% (wt/vol) donkey serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody and Lectin Staining  
5.1 Incubation with anti-Claudin-5 primary antibody (1:200 in staining buffer: PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100 + 5% DMSO + 3% donkey serum) and biotinylated Lectin (e.g., Lycopersicon esculentum, 1:100).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  

6 Washing  
6.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Repeat step 6.1 five times, changing solution every hour.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

7 Secondary Antibody and Streptavidin Conjugation  
7.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rat IgG (1:400) and Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated streptavidin (1:500) in staining buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  

8 Post-staining Washes  
8.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
8.2 Repeat step 8.1 five times, changing solution every hour.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

9 Dehydration (post-labeling)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation  
10.1 Incubation with dichloromethane (DCM, anhydrous).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with fresh dichloromethane (DCM, anhydrous).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with ethyl cinnamate (ECi, Sigma-Aldrich 112372).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
11.2 Incubation with fresh ethyl cinnamate (ECi).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

12 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
12.1 Transfer sample to glass vial filled with ethyl cinnamate and seal.(Temperature: RT, Time: Indefinite storage)  
12.2 Mount in ECi-compatible imaging chamber for light-sheet or confocal microscopy.(Temperature: RT, Time: Immediate imaging)

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Lectin (凝集素)+Alexa Fluor 647, Claudin-5+Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based, high-clearing-power method established for dense adult mouse brain tissue (5–12 mm scale) and preserves both Alexa Fluor 488 and Alexa Fluor 647 fluorescence with high compatibility, unlike iDISCO+ which quenches GFP/YFP and shows caution with lectins. Lectin (e.g., *Lycopersicon esculentum* or *Griffonia simplicifolia* isolectin B4) provides robust, perfusion-independent labeling of the entire vascular lumen—including tumor-associated vessels—while Claudin-5 specifically labels tight junctions of the blood-brain barrier, enabling assessment of barrier integrity across tumor core, edge, and peritumoral regions. FDISCO’s strong delipidation ensures deep antibody/lectin penetration into dense glioblastoma tissue without the morphological collapse seen in aqueous CUBIC protocols, and its RI-matching medium supports high-resolution light-sheet imaging of continuous vascular networks and tumor-vascular spatial relationships.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional but recommended for GBM autofluorescence reduction)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration (for immunolabeling)  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBT).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBT + 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum + 0.2% (wt/vol) sodium azide.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody and Lectin Staining  
5.1 Incubation with anti-Claudin-5 primary antibody (1:200 in PBT + 5% serum) and biotinylated or directly conjugated Lectin (e.g., *Lycopersicon esculentum* Lectin, 50 µg/mL) in same solution.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 5 days, gentle agitation)  

6 Washing  
6.1 Incubation with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Repeat wash step 6.1 five times, total Time: 6 hours  

7 Secondary Antibody Staining (if Lectin not pre-conjugated; here assumed pre-conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647)  
7.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 488–conjugated secondary antibody (1:500 in PBT + 5% serum) targeting host species of Claudin-5 primary.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 2 days, gentle agitation)  

8 Post-staining Washes  
8.1 Incubation with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
8.2 Repeat wash step 8.1 four times, total Time: 5 hours  

9 Dehydration (pre-clearing)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation  
10.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) : methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Repeat step 10.2 once.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) ethyl cinnamate (ECi).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
11.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) ECi.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

12 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
12.1 Store sample in 100% ECi at RT in light-protected container until imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite)  
12.2 Mount sample in glass capillary or imaging chamber filled with ECi for light-sheet or confocal microscopy.

**Chosen Method:** MACS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [内源GFP/YFP/tdTomato, MAP2 + Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires preservation of extremely weak endogenous fluorescent protein signals (e.g., GFP/YFP/tdTomato) over 6 months, which rules out solvent-based clearing methods (e.g., uDISCO, iDISCO+) that quench or destabilize FPs. Among aqueous, FP-compatible methods established for 3 mm brain blocks (T02_THICK_SLICE_0P5_3MM), MACS offers rapid clearing (~1–2 days), excellent FP retention, minimal tissue distortion, and strong compatibility with both endogenous FPs and antibody-based labeling. MAP2 is a well-validated pan-dendritic marker that complements sparse reporter neurons by revealing full dendritic arborization without requiring subtype-specific identity; conjugation to Alexa Fluor 488 ensures bright, photostable signal that survives long-term storage in MACS-RI matching solutions. MACS reagents are non-hazardous and support stable fluorescence preservation for ≥6 months when stored at 4 ℃ in the dark.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunolabeling (post-fixation, pre-clearing)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution: 10% (vol/vol) normal goat serum, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibody: anti-MAP2 (chicken or mouse monoclonal, 1:500 dilution) in blocking solution (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours with gentle agitation)  
1.3 Wash with PBS + 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (3 changes, 1 hour each) (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibody: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-host IgG (1:500 dilution) in blocking solution (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours with gentle agitation)  
1.5 Wash with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Tween-20 (3 changes, 1 hour each) (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  

2 Tissue Optical Clearing  
2.1 Incubation with MACS-C (clearing solution: 8% (wt/vol) N-methylnicotinamide, 10% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (vol/vol) glycerol, 0.1% (wt/vol) sodium azide in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours with gentle shaking)  
2.2 Wash with MACS-W (washing solution: 20% (vol/vol) glycerol, 0.1% (wt/vol) sodium azide in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

3 Refractive Index (RI) Matching and Long-Term Storage  
3.1 Incubation with MACS-R0 (20% (vol/vol) N-methylnicotinamide, 15% (wt/vol) sorbitol, 0.1% (wt/vol) sodium azide in PBS, RI ≈ 1.40) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with MACS-R1 (40% (vol/vol) N-methylnicotinamide, 30% (wt/vol) sorbitol, 0.1% (wt/vol) sodium azide in PBS, RI ≈ 1.48) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
3.3 Incubation with MACS-R2 (40% (vol/vol) N-methylnicotinamide, 50% (wt/vol) sorbitol, 0.1% (wt/vol) sodium azide in PBS, RI ≈ 1.51) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
3.4 Transfer sample to fresh MACS-R2 in a light-tight, sealed glass vial with minimal headspace (Temperature: 4 ℃, Storage Duration: up to 6 months)  

4 Imaging Preparation (prior to acquisition)  
4.1 Equilibrate sample in fresh MACS-R2 at RT for 2 hours before imaging to minimize thermal drift (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [NeuN (RBFOX3) + Alexa Fluor 488, MAP2 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** uDISCO is a high-clearing-power solvent-based method established for dense human clinical brain tissue (T09_HUMAN_DENSE_CLINICAL_BLOCK), enabling deep antibody penetration and effective delipidation of myelin-rich cortex. It is compatible with Alexa Fluor 488 and 647 conjugates—ideal for dual-pan-neuronal labeling targeting both nuclear (NeuN) and somatodendritic (MAP2) compartments of mature neurons, thereby increasing cell identification reliability across cortical layers and perilesional zones. Although uDISCO quenches endogenous FPs, our labeling uses robust synthetic fluorophores that remain stable. The method achieves high transparency in thick (5 mm) slices within days, supports 3D imaging by light-sheet/confocal microscopy, and provides sufficient morphological preservation for quantitative spatial analysis.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional for pigmented human tissue)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration (for immunolabeling)  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBT).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBT + 10% (vol/vol) normal goat serum (NGS) + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Incubation  
5.1 Incubation with anti-NeuN (mouse monoclonal, 1:500) and anti-MAP2 (rabbit polyclonal, 1:500) diluted in PBT + 5% NGS.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days, gentle agitation)  

6 Washing  
6.1 Incubation with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Repeat step 6.1 five times over 24 hours (total 6 washes).  

7 Secondary Antibody Incubation  
7.1 Incubation with goat anti-mouse IgG Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) and goat anti-rabbit IgG Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) in PBT + 5% NGS.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days, gentle agitation, protected from light)  

8 Post-labeling Washes  
8.1 Incubation with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
8.2 Repeat step 8.1 five times over 24 hours (total 6 washes, protected from light).  

9 Dehydration (post-labeling)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation  
10.1 Incubation with 66% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Repeat step 10.2 once.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
11.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

12 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
12.1 Transfer sample to glass vial filled with fresh DBE, seal tightly, and store at RT in the dark.(Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite until imaging)

MACS is an aqueous, fast, and low-toxicity clearing method established for ≤500 μm brain slices, fully compatible with endogenous GFP and Alexa Fluor dyes, and enables deep antibody penetration without quenching or significant tissue distortion. MAP2 is a well-validated dendritic cytoskeletal marker that labels the entire somatodendritic compartment, providing continuous dendritic backbone for accurate spine counting and length normalization, and pairs robustly with Alexa Fluor 568 under MACS conditions.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunostaining (post-fixation, pre-clearing)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution (5% normal goat serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

1.3 Wash with PBST (0.1% Tween-20 in PBS) three times, 30 minutes each (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes per wash)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibody Alexa Fluor 568-conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:1000 in blocking solution) (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  
1.5 Wash with PBST three times, 30 minutes each (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes per wash)  

2 Tissue Optical Clearing  
2.1 Incubation with MACS-R0 (20 vol% MXDA, 15% w/v sorbitol in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with MACS-R1 (40 vol% MXDA, 30% w/v sorbitol in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with MACS-R2 (40 vol% MXDA, 50% w/v sorbitol in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  

3 Refractive Index Matching and Storage  
3.1 Transfer slices into imaging chamber filled with MACS-R2 for immediate imaging, or store short-term at 4 ℃ in MACS-R2 (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: up to 48 hours)

**Chosen Method:** FOCM  
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP (内源), MAP2 + Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** The scientific goal requires rapid (<1 day) transparentization of 500 μm fixed mouse brain slices while preserving endogenous fluorescent protein signal (e.g., GFP/YFP from sparse neuronal labeling) and enabling high-resolution imaging of dendritic spines. FOCM is an aqueous, fast, low-toxicity clearing method specifically validated for thin brain slices (≤500 μm), with excellent preservation of endogenous fluorescence (GFP/YFP/tdTomato) and minimal morphological distortion—critical for accurate spine density quantification. To enhance dendritic shaft visualization and distinguish neuronal processes from background, we pair endogenous GFP (labeling sparse pyramidal neurons) with immunostaining against MAP2 (a dendrite-specific structural marker) conjugated to Alexa Fluor 568, which is compatible with FOCM and provides strong, stable signal without quenching. This dual-labeling strategy ensures robust identification of dendritic arbors and spines while meeting the tight experimental timeline.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunostaining (perform before clearing)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution (5% normal goat serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) to reduce non-specific binding.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibody against MAP2 (1:500 dilution in blocking solution).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
1.3 Wash with PBS + 0.3% Triton X-100 (3 × 30 minutes).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes per wash)  
1.4 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 568-conjugated secondary antibody (1:1000 in blocking solution).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, protected from light)  
1.5 Wash with PBS (3 × 30 minutes).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes per wash)  

2 Tissue Optical Clearing with FOCM  
2.1 Incubation with FOCM-A (25% (wt/vol) fructose, 10% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol in PBS, pH 7.4).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with FOCM-B (50% (wt/vol) fructose, 20% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol in PBS, pH 7.4).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with FOCM-C (75% (wt/vol) fructose, 30% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol in PBS, pH 7.4).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

3 Refractive Index Matching and Mounting  
3.1 Incubation with FOCM-M (88% (wt/vol) fructose, 35% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol in PBS, final RI ≈ 1.46).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Transfer slice to imaging chamber and mount in FOCM-M under a coverslip, sealed with nail polish to prevent evaporation.(Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or storage at 4 ℃ for up to 48 hours)

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [NeuN (RBFOX3) + Alexa Fluor 488, MAP2 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** The problem involves 3 mm thick, densely fixed human cortical tissue where deep antibody penetration failed with standard PBS-based labeling. uDISCO is a high-clearing-power solvent-based method established for dense human clinical brain blocks (T09_HUMAN_DENSE_CLINICAL_BLOCK), enabling robust delipidation and deep antibody penetration. It is compatible with Alexa Fluor 488 and 647 conjugates—ideal for dual mature neuron labeling—and avoids reliance on endogenous fluorescence (which is absent in postmortem fixed tissue). 9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

10.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)

12.1 Store sample immersed in DBE in light-protected glass vial at RT until imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: indefinite)

**Chosen Method:** iDISCO+  
**Chosen Labeling:** [NeuN (RBFOX3) + Alexa Fluor 488, MAP2 + Alexa Fluor 647]

Endogenous fluorescence is not required; instead, we use two pan-neuronal structural markers—NeuN for mature neuronal nuclei and MAP2 for dendritic arbors—to enable comprehensive 3D mapping of mature neuron distribution, layer-specific localization, and density analysis. Both primary antibodies are well-validated in human postmortem tissue, and their conjugation to Alexa Fluor 488/647 ensures robust signal retention through iDISCO+’s organic solvent steps.

3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBST + 20% (vol/vol) DMSO + 0.3 M glycine.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)

**Chosen Method:** uDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [NeuN (RBFOX3) + Alexa Fluor 488, MAP2 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** The problem involves 3 mm thick, densely fixed human cortical tissue where deep antibody penetration failed with standard PBS-based labeling. uDISCO is a high-clearing-power solvent-based method established for dense human clinical brain blocks (T09_HUMAN_DENSE_CLINICAL_BLOCK), enabling deep antibody penetration and efficient lipid removal while maintaining structural integrity sufficient for layer-specific neuron mapping. It is compatible with Alexa Fluor 488 and 647 conjugates—robust synthetic fluorophores resistant to organic solvents—and supports dual mature neuron labeling: NeuN (nuclear marker of post-mitotic neurons) and MAP2 (dendritic/somatic cytoskeletal marker). This dual-target strategy enhances reliability of mature neuron identification in deep layers by co-localizing nuclear and somatic signals, overcoming the limitation of single-marker dropout. Endogenous FPs are not used per constraints, and DAPI/Hoechst are avoided due to compatibility cautions with neuronal markers in solvent clearing.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Delipidation and Bleaching  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration (for antibody labeling)  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Blocking and Primary Antibody Incubation  
4.1 Incubation with blocking solution (PBST + 10% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum + 5% (wt/vol) DMSO).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 6 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-NeuN (mouse monoclonal, 1:500) and anti-MAP2 (rabbit polyclonal, 1:250) diluted in PBST + 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum + 5% (wt/vol) DMSO.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 7 days with gentle agitation)  

5 Washing  
5.1 Incubation with PBST.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
5.2 Repeat PBST wash.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
5.3 Repeat PBST wash.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

6 Secondary Antibody Incubation  
6.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies: donkey anti-mouse Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) and donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) diluted in PBST + 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum + 5% (wt/vol) DMSO.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days with gentle agitation)  

7 Post-labeling Washing  
7.1 Incubation with PBST.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
7.2 Repeat PBST wash.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
7.3 Repeat PBST wash.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

8 Dehydration (post-labeling)  
8.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** FOCM  
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP (endogenous), MAP2 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** FOCM is an aqueous, rapid, and low-toxicity clearing method specifically validated for ≤500 μm brain slices, preserving endogenous fluorescent proteins (e.g., GFP) and fine dendritic structures with minimal distortion—critical for accurate spine density quantification. It achieves refractive index (RI) matching within hours, enabling same-day imaging. The dual-labeling strategy uses endogenous GFP to label spines (e.g., in Thy1-GFP-M mice) and immunostaining against MAP2 (a dendritic shaft marker) conjugated to Alexa Fluor 647 to delineate dendritic arbor geometry, allowing precise selection of analysis segments and normalization of spine counts per unit dendrite length. Both fluorophores are fully compatible with FOCM, and the protocol integrates antibody penetration efficiently without quenching.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunostaining (if not pre-labeled)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution (5% normal goat serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) to reduce non-specific binding. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibody anti-MAP2 (1:500 in blocking solution). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
1.3 Wash with PBS + 0.3% Triton X-100 (3 × 30 min). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1.5 hours total)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibody Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:800 in blocking solution). (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  
1.5 Wash with PBS (3 × 30 min). (Temperature: RT, Time: 1.5 hours total)  

2 Tissue Optical Clearing with FOCM  
2.1 Incubation with FOCM-A (25% (wt/vol) fructose, 10% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol, 0.1 M phosphate buffer, pH 7.4). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with FOCM-B (40% (wt/vol) fructose, 15% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol, 0.1 M phosphate buffer, pH 7.4). (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with FOCM-C (63% (wt/vol) fructose, 20% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol, 0.1 M phosphate buffer, pH 7.4; final RI ≈ 1.45). (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours)  

3 Refractive Index Matching and Mounting  
3.1 Transfer slices into fresh FOCM-C for final equilibration. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Mount samples between #1.5H coverslips using FOCM-C as immersion medium in a spacer-defined imaging chamber. (Temperature: RT, Time: 10 minutes)  

Total processing time: ~24 hours (including overnight immunostaining); if samples are already GFP+/MAP2-stained, clearing and mounting can be completed in <8 hours.

**Chosen Method:** MACS  
**Chosen Labeling:** [GFP (内源) + MAP2 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** The original TDE protocol failed due to excessive concentration (100% directly), lack of gradual RI matching, and methanol-based fixation that likely compromised membrane integrity and spine morphology. For 500 μm brain slices requiring endogenous FP preservation, high-resolution dendritic spine visualization, minimal distortion, and completion within 1 day, an aqueous, non-denaturing clearing method is essential. MACS is established for thin brain slices (≤500 μm), preserves GFP/YFP/tdTomato fluorescence, enables deep antibody penetration, induces negligible shrinkage, and achieves clearing in <24 h. MAP2 is a well-validated structural marker for dendritic shafts and branches that complements sparse endogenous GFP labeling of pyramidal neurons, enabling accurate dendritic skeleton reconstruction for spine density normalization. Alexa Fluor 647 is compatible with MACS and provides far-red signal with minimal crosstalk and high photostability for high-resolution confocal or light-sheet imaging.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Fixation Re-evaluation and Pre-Clearing Wash  
1.1 Incubation with 4% (wt/vol) paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS for post-fixation to reverse methanol-induced artifacts (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Wash with PBS containing 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST) (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 30 minutes)  

2 Immunolabeling for Dendritic Skeleton  
2.1 Blocking with blocking buffer (5% normal goat serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with primary antibody anti-MAP2 (1:500 in blocking buffer) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  
2.3 Wash with PBST (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with secondary antibody Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-mouse/rabbit IgG (1:800 in blocking buffer) (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  
2.5 Wash with PBST (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 × 1 hour)  

3 Optical Clearing with MACS  
3.1 Incubation with MACS-R0 (20 vol% N-methyldiethanolamine (MXDA), 15% w/v sorbitol in PBS, pH 7.4) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with MACS-R1 (40 vol% MXDA, 30% w/v sorbitol in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
3.3 Incubation with MACS-R2 (40 vol% MXDA, 50% w/v sorbitol in PBS) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

4 Refractive Index Matching and Imaging Preparation  
4.1 Equilibration in final imaging medium: MACS-R2 (same as 3.3) for at least 30 minutes before imaging (Temperature: RT, Time: ≥30 minutes)  
4.2 Mount sample in glass-bottom dish or chamber filled with MACS-R2 for immediate confocal or light-sheet microscopy (no additional dehydration or solvent steps required)

**Chosen Method:** Ce3D  
**Chosen Labeling:** [β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) + Alexa Fluor 488, Sox10 + Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** Ce3D is an aqueous, low-toxicity clearing method established for small whole embryonic samples (T03 tier), offering excellent preservation of tissue morphology with minimal shrinkage—critical for accurate 3D reconstruction of delicate early neural projections. It supports deep penetration of antibodies and is fully compatible with Alexa Fluor 488 and 568 conjugates. The dual-labeling strategy targets β-III Tubulin (TUJ1), a pan-neuronal marker labeling all axons and early neurites, and Sox10, a transcription factor specifically expressed in neural crest–derived lineages including cranial and spinal peripheral glia and some neuronal precursors, enabling discrimination between central and peripheral neural elements. This combination provides comprehensive coverage of cranial/spinal nerves and their peripheral branches while preserving spatial fidelity for directional and branching analysis.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunolabeling (performed post-fixation, pre-clearing)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution: 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-β-III Tubulin (TUJ1, 1:500) and anti-Sox10 (1:200) in antibody dilution buffer (1% NDS, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 5 days with gentle agitation)  
1.3 Wash with PBST (0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS): 6 changes over 2 days (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours per wash)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488–conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 568–conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:500) in antibody dilution buffer (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 3 days with gentle agitation)  
1.5 Wash with PBST: 6 changes over 2 days (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours per wash)  

2 Tissue Optical Clearing  
2.1 Incubation with Ce3D-Clearing Solution A: 25% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol, 10% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (vol/vol) glycerol in 0.1 M phosphate buffer, pH 7.5 (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with Ce3D-Clearing Solution B: 30% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol, 20% (wt/vol) urea, 20% (vol/vol) glycerol in 0.1 M phosphate buffer, pH 7.5 (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with Ce3D-Clearing Solution C: 40% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 30% (vol/vol) glycerol in 0.1 M phosphate buffer, pH 7.5 (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  

3 Refractive Index (RI) Matching  
3.1 Incubation with Ce3D-RI Matching Solution: 60% (wt/vol) iodixanol (OptiPrep), 15% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol, 10% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (vol/vol) glycerol in 0.1 M phosphate buffer, pH 7.5 (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours)  

4 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
4.1 Transfer sample to imaging chamber filled with Ce3D-RI Matching Solution (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or storage at 4 ℃ for up to 2 weeks)

**Chosen Method:** Ce3D  
**Chosen Labeling:** [β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) + Alexa Fluor 488, PGP9.5 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** Ce3D is an aqueous, low-toxicity clearing method established for small whole embryonic samples (T03 tier), offering excellent preservation of tissue morphology with minimal shrinkage—critical for accurate 3D reconstruction of delicate early neural projections. It supports deep penetration of antibodies and is fully compatible with Alexa Fluor dyes. The dual-marker strategy targets both early differentiating neurons (β-III Tubulin/TUJ1) and pan-neuronal structures including mature nerve bundles (PGP9.5), enabling simultaneous visualization of nascent neurites and established cranial/spinal/peripheral nerve tracts. Extended antibody incubation and rigorous washing are incorporated to overcome prior issues of weak signal and high background.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Antibody Labeling (post-fixation, pre-clearing)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution: 10% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-β-III Tubulin (TUJ1, 1:500) and anti-PGP9.5 (1:400) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 5 days with gentle agitation)  
1.3 Wash with PBST (0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS): 6 changes over 3 days (each wash ≥6 hours). (Temperature: RT, Time: total 72 hours)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:500) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 5 days with gentle agitation)  
1.5 Wash with PBST: 6 changes over 3 days (each wash ≥6 hours). (Temperature: RT, Time: total 72 hours)  

2 Tissue Optical Clearing (Ce3D protocol)  
2.1 Incubation with Ce3D-A1: 25% (wt/vol) N-methylnicotinamide, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (wt/vol) sucrose, 0.1 M Tris-HCl pH 8.0. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with Ce3D-A2: 50% (wt/vol) N-methylnicotinamide, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (wt/vol) sucrose, 0.1 M Tris-HCl pH 8.0. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with Ce3D-B: 50% (wt/vol) N-methylnicotinamide, 50% (wt/vol) iodixanol, 0.1 M Tris-HCl pH 8.0. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  

3 Refractive Index Matching and Storage  
3.1 Transfer sample to imaging chamber filled with Ce3D-B (RI ≈ 1.48). (Temperature: RT, Time: ≥2 hours before imaging)  
3.2 Store long-term at 4 ℃ in Ce3D-B in the dark. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: indefinite)

**Chosen Method:** Ce3D  
**Chosen Labeling:** [β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) + Alexa Fluor 488, Sox10 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** Ce3D is an aqueous-based clearing method established for small whole embryonic samples (T03 tier), offering excellent preservation of endogenous and antibody-based fluorescence, minimal tissue distortion, and deep penetration of antibodies—critical for tracing delicate early neural projections across the entire E12.5 embryo (~8–10 mm). The dual-labeling strategy uses β-III Tubulin (TUJ1), a pan-neuronal marker labeling all axons and neurites, combined with Sox10, a transcription factor specifically expressed in neural crest-derived lineages including cranial and peripheral glia and Schwann cell precursors. This pairing enables reliable discrimination of neuronal processes (TUJ1) from their associated glial scaffolds (Sox10), enhancing confidence in identifying true nerve bundles versus background or non-neural structures during 3D reconstruction. Both Alexa Fluor 488 and 647 are fully compatible with Ce3D and provide spectrally separable, photostable signals ideal for light-sheet imaging.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunolabeling (performed post-fixation, pre-clearing)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution: 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-β-III Tubulin (TUJ1, e.g., BioLegend 801201, 1:500) and anti-Sox10 (e.g., R&D Systems AF2864, 1:250) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 5 days with gentle agitation)  
1.3 Washing with PBST (PBS + 0.5% Triton X-100): 6 changes over 3 days (each wash: 12 hours). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: total 72 hours)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: donkey anti-mouse IgG Alexa Fluor 488 (1:500) and donkey anti-goat IgG Alexa Fluor 647 (1:500) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 4 days with gentle agitation)  
1.5 Washing with PBST: 6 changes over 3 days (each wash: 12 hours). (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: total 72 hours)  

2 Tissue Optical Clearing (Ce3D protocol)  
2.1 Incubation with Ce3D-A1: 10% (wt/vol) N-methylnicotinamide (NMN), 10% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (wt/vol) sucrose, 0.1% (wt/vol) sodium deoxycholate in distilled water. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with Ce3D-A2: 25% (wt/vol) NMN, 25% (wt/vol) urea, 25% (wt/vol) sucrose, 0.1% (wt/vol) sodium deoxycholate in distilled water. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with Ce3D-B: 50% (wt/vol) NMN, 30% (wt/vol) urea, 30% (wt/vol) sucrose in distilled water. (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  

3 Refractive Index Matching  
3.1 Incubation with Ce3D-RI matching solution: 88% (wt/vol) iodixanol (OptiPrep), adjusted to RI ≈ 1.47 with distilled water. (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

4 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
4.1 Transfer sample into fresh Ce3D-RI matching solution in glass-bottom imaging chamber or matched cuvette. (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or storage at 4 ℃ for up to 2 weeks)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [β-III Tubulin (TUJ1) + Alexa Fluor 488, Neurofilament + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based clearing method optimized for whole-mount embryos (8–10 mm) that provides strong lipid removal, high refractive index matching, and excellent preservation of exogenous fluorophores like Alexa Fluor dyes—critical for deep imaging of both mature nerve bundles and fine early neurites. It outperforms aqueous methods in clearing speed and penetration depth for dense embryonic tissue while maintaining signal integrity of antibody-conjugated dyes. The dual-labeling strategy uses β-III Tubulin (TUJ1), a pan-neuronal marker labeling all developing axons including nascent neurites, and Neurofilament, which enriches in more mature, bundled axons (e.g., cranial/spinal nerves), enabling simultaneous visualization of early projections and established tracts. Both primary antibodies are well-established for embryonic neural tissue and compatible with FDISCO’s organic solvent workflow.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Antibody Labeling (post-fixation, pre-clearing)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution: 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-β-III Tubulin (TUJ1, 1:500) and anti-Neurofilament (clone 2H3 or equivalent, 1:300) in antibody dilution buffer (1% NDS, 0.2% Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 5 days with gentle agitation)  
1.3 Wash with PBST (0.2% Triton X-100 in PBS): 6 changes over 2 days (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours per wash)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-chicken or anti-rabbit IgG (as appropriate to host species, 1:500) in antibody dilution buffer (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 3 days with gentle agitation)  
1.5 Wash with PBST: 6 changes over 2 days (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours per wash)  

2 Dehydration  
2.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
2.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
2.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

3 Delipidation and Bleaching  
3.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (prepare fresh: 1 part 30% H₂O₂ + 5 parts methanol) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours, protected from light)  
3.2 Wash with 100% methanol: 2 changes (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes each)  

4 Rehydration (for optional post-bleach nuclear counterstain; skip if not needed)  
4.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
4.5 Incubation with PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

5 Dehydration (post-rehydration, if performed)  
5.1 Repeat steps 2.1–2.6 exactly as above  

6 Clearing and Refractive Index Matching  
6.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) : methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM (fresh) (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) ethyl cinnamate (ECi) (Sigma-Aldrich, 112302) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
6.5 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) ECi (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

7 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
7.1 Transfer embryo to glass vial filled with fresh ECi and seal (Temperature: RT, long-term storage)  
7.2 Mount in ECi-compatible imaging chamber for light-sheet or confocal microscopy (no additional RI adjustment needed; ECi RI ≈ 1.558)

**Chosen Method:** FlyClear  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Bruchpilot (BRP/nc82)+Alexa Fluor 647, Synapsin+Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** FlyClear is an aqueous-based, insect-optimized clearing method that preserves endogenous fluorescence and provides excellent morphological integrity for small, chitinous samples like Drosophila heads (~0.5 mm). It enables deep antibody penetration without harsh solvents, minimizing tissue distortion—critical for accurate 3D mapping of synaptic architecture. Bruchpilot (nc82) is a well-established marker for the presynaptic active zone in Drosophila, while Synapsin labels synaptic vesicle clusters; dual labeling with spectrally distinct Alexa Fluor dyes (488 and 647) allows clear discrimination of active zones versus vesicle pools. Both Alexa Fluor 488 and 647 are fully compatible with FlyClear and resistant to quenching, ensuring high signal fidelity during imaging.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunolabeling  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution: 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum, 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: mouse anti-Bruchpilot (nc82, 1:50) and rabbit anti-Synapsin (1:200) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
1.3 Wash with PBST (0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS): 3 changes, 1 hour each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: goat anti-mouse IgG Alexa Fluor 647 (1:400) and goat anti-rabbit IgG Alexa Fluor 488 (1:400) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
1.5 Wash with PBST: 4 changes, 1 hour each. (Temperature: RT, Time: 4 hours total)  

2 Tissue Optical Clearing  
2.1 Incubation with FlyClear Solution A (20% (wt/vol) fructose, 10% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol in PBS, pH 7.5). (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with FlyClear Solution B (40% (wt/vol) fructose, 20% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol in PBS, pH 7.5). (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with FlyClear Solution C (60% (wt/vol) fructose, 30% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol in PBS, pH 7.5). (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Refractive Index Matching and Mounting  
3.1 Incubation with final RI matching solution: FlyClear Imaging Buffer (80% (wt/vol) fructose, 30% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol, 0.1% (vol/vol) Tween-20 in PBS, RI ≈ 1.45). (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  
3.2 Transfer sample into glass-bottom imaging chamber filled with FlyClear Imaging Buffer for light-sheet or confocal microscopy. (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or storage at 4 ℃ for up to 1 week)

**Chosen Method:** FlyClear  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Bruchpilot (BRP/nc82)+Alexa Fluor 488, Synapsin+Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** FlyClear is an aqueous-based, insect-optimized clearing method that preserves endogenous fluorescence and provides excellent morphological integrity for small, chitinous samples like whole Drosophila heads or brains (~0.5 mm). It enables deep antibody penetration without harsh organic solvents, minimizing tissue distortion—critical for precise 3D quantification of synaptic structures. Bruchpilot (nc82) is a well-established marker for the presynaptic active zone in Drosophila, while Synapsin labels synaptic vesicle clusters; dual labeling with spectrally distinct Alexa Fluor dyes (488 and 568) ensures high signal-to-noise, compatibility with FlyClear, and clear spatial resolution of active zones versus vesicle pools for circuit-level synapse mapping.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Immunolabeling  
1.1 Incubation with blocking solution (5% normal goat serum, 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS) to reduce non-specific binding. (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: mouse anti-Bruchpilot (nc82, 1:50) and rabbit anti-Synapsin (1:200) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
1.3 Washing with PBST (0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS), 6 changes over 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours total)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: goat anti-mouse IgG Alexa Fluor 488 (1:400) and goat anti-rabbit IgG Alexa Fluor 568 (1:400) in blocking solution. (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
1.5 Washing with PBST, 6 changes over 24 hours. (Temperature: RT, Time: 24 hours total)  

2 Tissue Optical Clearing  
2.1 Incubation with FlyClear Solution A (20% (wt/vol) fructose, 10% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol, 0.1 M phosphate buffer, pH 7.4). (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with FlyClear Solution B (40% (wt/vol) fructose, 20% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol, 0.1 M phosphate buffer, pH 7.4). (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with FlyClear Solution C (60% (wt/vol) fructose, 30% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol, 0.1 M phosphate buffer, pH 7.4). (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
2.4 Incubation with final RI-matching solution: FlyClear Imaging Buffer (80% (wt/vol) fructose, 30% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol, 0.1 M phosphate buffer, pH 7.4, RI ≈ 1.45). (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  

3 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
3.1 Transfer cleared sample into glass-bottom imaging dish filled with FlyClear Imaging Buffer. (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate use or store at 4 ℃ up to 1 week)  
3.2 Seal dish to prevent evaporation and equilibrate at RT for 1 hour before light-sheet or confocal imaging. (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

model_response:
**Chosen Method:** FlyClear  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Bruchpilot (BRP/nc82)+Alexa Fluor 488, Synapsin+Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** FlyClear is an aqueous, insect-optimized clearing method specifically validated for Drosophila heads and brains, preserving fine synaptic structures while effectively clearing the chitinous cuticle—a key failure point in the original SeeDB2 attempt. It maintains endogenous fluorescence and is compatible with immunolabeling, enabling high-fidelity dual-channel imaging of synaptic compartments. Bruchpilot (nc82) is a well-established marker for the presynaptic active zone in Drosophila, while Synapsin labels synaptic vesicle clusters adjacent to but distinct from active zones, allowing functional domain discrimination. Both are robustly detected with Alexa Fluor conjugates, which are fully compatible with FlyClear’s aqueous, non-denaturing environment and provide strong signal-to-noise for 3D reconstruction.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Rehydration and Cuticle Permeabilization  
1.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
1.2 Incubation with 30% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
1.3 Incubation with PBS only (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
1.4 Incubation with FlyClear-P (0.5% (wt/vol) saponin, 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

2 Immunolabeling  
2.1 Blocking with FlyClear-B (5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum, 0.5% (wt/vol) saponin, 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 6 hours)  
2.2 Primary antibody incubation: mouse anti-nc82 (1:50) + rabbit anti-Synapsin (1:200) in FlyClear-B (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  
2.3 Washing with FlyClear-W (0.5% (wt/vol) saponin, 0.1% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 6 hours × 3 changes)  
2.4 Secondary antibody incubation: goat anti-mouse Alexa Fluor 488 (1:300) + goat anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 568 (1:300) in FlyClear-B (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours, protected from light)  
2.5 Final washing with FlyClear-W (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 12 hours × 3 changes, protected from light)  

3 Optical Clearing and Refractive Index Matching  
3.1 Incubation with FlyClear-C1 (25% (wt/vol) fructose, 10% (wt/vol) sucrose, 0.5% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol in 0.1 M phosphate buffer, pH 7.4) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
3.2 Incubation with FlyClear-C2 (50% (wt/vol) fructose, 20% (wt/vol) sucrose, 0.5% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol in 0.1 M phosphate buffer, pH 7.4) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
3.3 Incubation with FlyClear-C3 (80% (wt/vol) fructose, 0.5% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol in 0.1 M phosphate buffer, pH 7.4) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  

4 Mounting and Imaging Preparation  
4.1 Transfer sample into glass-bottom imaging dish or capillary tube filled with FlyClear-C3 (Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or storage at 4 ℃ up to 1 week, protected from light)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Osx (Osterix)+Alexa Fluor 488, Osteocalcin+Alexa Fluor 568, DAPI]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based clearing method specifically validated for dense hard tissues like postnatal mouse calvaria (T07_HARD_TISSUE_BONE_TOOTH_COCHLEA), offering strong delipidation and high refractive index matching essential for deep imaging of mineralized bone. It enables excellent antibody penetration into thick (~2 mm) bone blocks while preserving fine cellular morphology with minimal distortion compared to other organic solvent methods. Although FDISCO quenches endogenous fluorescent proteins, our labeling strategy uses immunofluorescence against two stage-specific osteoblast lineage markers—Osx (early committed osteoprogenitors) and Osteocalcin (late differentiated osteoblasts)—conjugated to photostable Alexa Fluor dyes compatible with FDISCO. DAPI provides nuclear counterstaining to contextualize cell positions within the suture architecture. This dual-marker approach allows precise 3D mapping of osteogenic progression across the suture margin, osteogenic front, and adjacent bone plates during P7 cranial growth.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional but recommended for bone autofluorescence reduction)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (prepared fresh from 30% H₂O₂ stock).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration (for immunolabeling)  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with permeabilization buffer (0.5% Triton X-100, 10% normal goat serum in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 6 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-Osx (1:200) and anti-Osteocalcin (1:200) diluted in antibody dilution buffer (0.2% Triton X-100, 5% normal goat serum in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours with gentle agitation)  

6 Washing  
6.1 Incubation with washing buffer (0.2% Tween-20 in PBS).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Repeat step 6.1 five times, changing buffer each time.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

7 Secondary Antibody Staining  
7.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 568-conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:500), plus DAPI (1 µg/mL), all diluted in antibody dilution buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours with gentle agitation in dark)  

8 Post-staining Washes  
8.1 Incubation with washing buffer (0.2% Tween-20 in PBS).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
8.2 Repeat step 8.1 four times, changing buffer each time.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

9 Dehydration (pre-clearing)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Delipidation and Clearing  
10.1 Incubation with dichloromethane (DCM, anhydrous, ≥99.8%).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with fresh dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with benzyl alcohol:benzyl benzoate (BABB, 1:2 vol/vol mixture).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
11.2 Incubation with fresh BABB (1:2).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

12 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
12.1 Transfer sample to glass vial filled with fresh BABB and seal with parafilm.(Temperature: RT, Time: Indefinite storage in dark)  
12.2 Mount sample in BABB-compatible imaging chamber for light-sheet or confocal microscopy without additional steps.

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Osx (Osterix)+Alexa Fluor 488, Osteocalcin+Alexa Fluor 568]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based clearing method specifically validated for hard mineralized tissues like P7 mouse calvaria, offering strong delipidation and high refractive index matching essential for dense bone. It enables deep antibody penetration while effectively reducing bone autofluorescence—critical for distinguishing true signal from background in the suture region. Although FDISCO quenches endogenous fluorescent proteins, our targets (early osteoprogenitors marked by Osx and mature osteoblasts marked by Osteocalcin) are best detected via immunostaining with bright, photostable Alexa Fluor dyes, which are fully compatible with FDISCO. This dual-marker strategy allows precise spatial mapping of osteolineage progression across suture zones with minimal morphological distortion.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Delipidation and Bleaching  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes MeOH).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBST).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Immunostaining  
4.1 Incubation with blocking solution (PBST + 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum + 0.2% (wt/vol) sodium azide).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-Osx (1:200) and anti-Osteocalcin (1:200) diluted in blocking solution.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  
4.3 Washing with PBST (3 changes, 1 hour each).(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  
4.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:400) and Alexa Fluor 568-conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:400) in blocking solution.(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.5 Washing with PBST (3 changes, 1 hour each).(Temperature: RT, Time: 3 hours total)  

5 Dehydration (post-staining)  
5.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
5.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
5.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
5.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
5.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
5.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

6 Clearing and Refractive Index Matching  
6.1 Incubation with 1:2 (vol/vol) mixture of dichloromethane (DCM) and methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM (fresh).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
6.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) ethyl cinnamate (ECi).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

7 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
7.1 Transfer sample to glass vial filled with fresh ECi for long-term storage at RT in the dark.(Temperature: RT, Time: Indefinite)  
7.2 Mount sample in ECi-filled imaging chamber compatible with light-sheet or confocal microscopy, ensuring no air bubbles.(Temperature: RT, Time: Immediate imaging)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Osx (Osterix)+Alexa Fluor 488, Osteocalcin+Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based, high-clearing-power method specifically validated for dense hard tissues like postnatal mouse calvarial bone (T07_HARD_TISSUE_BONE_TOOTH_COCHLEA tier). It enables deep antibody penetration into mineralized tissue while preserving antigenicity for robust immunolabeling—critical for distinguishing early (Osx+) and mature (Osteocalcin+) osteoblast populations across the suture microenvironment. Although FDISCO quenches endogenous fluorescent proteins, our labeling strategy uses exogenous Alexa Fluor–conjugated secondary antibodies, which are fully compatible. The method’s relatively fast processing time (~5–7 days) and high refractive index matching support high-resolution 3D imaging of cellular and vascular architecture in the suture niche.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Delipidation and Bleaching  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with permeabilization buffer (0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) DMSO, 0.3 M glycine in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
4.2 Incubation with blocking buffer (0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 10% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 0.02% (wt/vol) sodium azide in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-Osx (1:200) and anti-Osteocalcin (1:200) diluted in antibody dilution buffer (0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100, 5% (vol/vol) normal donkey serum, 0.02% (wt/vol) sodium azide in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours)  

6 Washing  
6.1 Incubation with wash buffer (0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS) with gentle shaking.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
6.2 Repeat wash buffer incubation.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

7 Secondary Antibody Staining  
7.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488–conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:500) and Alexa Fluor 647–conjugated anti-mouse IgG (1:500) in antibody dilution buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  

8 Post-staining Washes  
8.1 Incubation with wash buffer (0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
8.2 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

9 Dehydration (post-immunostaining)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Refractive Index Matching  
10.1 Incubation with 50% (vol/vol) dichloromethane (DCM) in hexane.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) DCM (fresh).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.4 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

11 Imaging Preparation  
11.1 Transfer sample to glass-bottom imaging dish filled with fresh DBE for light-sheet or confocal microscopy.(Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or storage at RT in dark for up to 1 week)
