**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Osx (Osterix)+Alexa Fluor 488, Osteocalcin+Alexa Fluor 568, TO-PRO-3]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based clearing method established for hard tissues like P7 mouse calvarial bone, offering strong delipidation and high refractive index matching essential for deep imaging in mineralized tissue. It enables excellent antibody penetration into dense bone while preserving fine cellular morphology with minimal distortion compared to other solvent methods. Although it quenches endogenous fluorescent proteins, our labeling strategy uses immunofluorescence with Alexa Fluor dyes—both compatible with FDISCO—and nuclear counterstain TO-PRO-3 (superior to DAPI/Hoechst in bone due to reduced autofluorescence interference). Osx marks early osteoprogenitors in the suture mesenchyme and osteogenic fronts, while Osteocalcin labels mature osteoblasts embedded near mineralized bone; this dual-target approach directly addresses the spatial comparison goal across suture zones.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional but recommended for bone autofluorescence control)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ + 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration (for immunostaining)  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 10% (vol/vol) normal goat serum.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with anti-Osx (Osterix) rabbit polyclonal antibody (1:200) and anti-Osteocalcin goat polyclonal antibody (1:200) in PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  

6 Washing  
6.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Repeat step 6.1 three more times (total 4 washes).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)  

7 Secondary Antibody Staining  
7.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated donkey anti-rabbit IgG (1:400) and Alexa Fluor 568-conjugated donkey anti-goat IgG (1:400) in PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

8 Washing  
8.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
8.2 Repeat step 8.1 three more times (total 4 washes).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour each)  

9 Nuclear Counterstaining  
9.1 Incubation with TO-PRO-3 iodide (1 µM) in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

10 Final Washing  
10.1 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

11 Dehydration (pre-clearing)  
11.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
11.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
11.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
11.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
11.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
11.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

12 Delipidation and Clearing  
12.1 Incubation with dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
12.2 Incubation with fresh dichloromethane (DCM).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

13 Refractive Index Matching  
13.1 Incubation with benzyl alcohol:benzyl benzoate (BABB, 1:2 vol/vol).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
13.2 Incubation with fresh BABB (1:2 vol/vol).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

14 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
14.1 Transfer sample to glass vial filled with BABB (1:2 vol/vol) and seal tightly.(Temperature: RT, Time: Indefinite storage; image within 1 week for optimal signal)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [TH + Alexa Fluor 488, CD31 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based, high-clearing-power method specifically validated for dense hard tissues like intact mouse bone (T07_HARD_TISSUE_BONE_TOOTH_COCHLEA). It enables deep antibody penetration into the mineralized femur while preserving fluorescence of synthetic dyes such as Alexa Fluor conjugates. Endogenous fluorescent proteins are quenched in FDISCO, so we use immunolabeling with target-specific primary antibodies: tyrosine hydroxylase (TH) to label sympathetic nerve fibers and CD31 (PECAM1) to label vascular endothelial structures—both critical for mapping neuro-vascular spatial relationships in the hematopoietic stem cell niche. Alexa Fluor 488 and 647 are compatible with FDISCO and provide spectrally distinct, photostable signals suitable for light-sheet or confocal 3D imaging.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

2 Bleaching (optional but recommended for bone autofluorescence reduction)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in 100% methanol (prepared fresh: 1 vol 30% H₂O₂ + 5 vol MeOH) (Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration (for immunolabeling)  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% Triton X-100 (PBST) (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBST + 10% (vol/vol) normal goat serum + 0.5% (wt/vol) sodium azide (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with anti-TH (rabbit or mouse monoclonal, 1:200) and anti-CD31 (rat monoclonal, 1:100) diluted in PBST + 5% normal goat serum + 0.5% sodium azide (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 72 hours with gentle agitation)  

6 Washing  
6.1 Incubation with PBST (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  
6.2 Incubation with fresh PBST (Temperature: RT, Time: 6 hours)  
6.3 Incubation with fresh PBST (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

7 Secondary Antibody Staining  
7.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-host-IgG (for TH, 1:400) and Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-rat-IgG (for CD31, 1:400) in PBST + 5% normal goat serum + 0.5% sodium azide (protected from light) (Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours with gentle agitation)  

8 Post-staining Washes  
8.1 Incubation with PBST (protected from light) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
8.2 Incubation with fresh PBST (protected from light) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
8.3 Incubation with fresh PBST (protected from light) (Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  

9 Dehydration (pre-clearing)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS (Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

10 Delipidation and Clearing  
10.1 Incubation with 1:2 mixture of dichloromethane (DCM) and 100% methanol (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with 100% DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Incubation with fresh 100% DCM (Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

11 Refractive Index Matching  
11.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE, Sigma-Aldrich 108014) (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
11.2 Incubation with fresh 100% DBE (Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

12 Storage and Imaging Preparation  
12.1 Transfer sample to glass vial filled with fresh DBE and store at RT protected from light until imaging (stable for ≥1 week)  
12.2 Mount in DBE-compatible imaging chamber for light-sheet or confocal microscopy (RI ≈ 1.56)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [TH + Alexa Fluor 568, CD31 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** FDISCO is a solvent-based, high-clearing-power method specifically validated for dense hard tissues like intact mouse femur, enabling deep antibody penetration into the bone marrow cavity while preserving fine neural and vascular structures. It efficiently removes lipids and decalcifies minimally fixed bone without severe distortion, critical for spatial analysis of the hematopoietic niche. Although it quenches endogenous fluorescent proteins, our targets—sympathetic nerve fibers (marked by tyrosine hydroxylase, TH) and vascular endothelium (marked by CD31/PECAM1)—are robustly labeled via immunostaining with bright, photostable Alexa Fluor dyes compatible with FDISCO. Alexa Fluor 568 and 647 exhibit excellent signal retention in FDISCO and allow spectral separation for dual-channel 3D imaging of nerve-vessel spatial relationships across central marrow, endosteal, and metaphyseal zones.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional, if endogenous pigment present)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ + 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Primary Antibody Staining  
3.1 Rehydrate samples through descending methanol series: 80%, 60%, 40%, 20% methanol in PBS (1 hour each, RT).  
3.2 Incubation with blocking solution (5% normal donkey serum, 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
3.3 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-TH (1:200) and anti-CD31 (1:100) in blocking solution.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days, gentle shaking)  

4 Wash  
4.1 Wash with PBST (0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS), 3 changes.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours total)  

5 Secondary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with secondary antibodies: donkey anti-rabbit Alexa Fluor 568 (1:300) and donkey anti-rat Alexa Fluor 647 (1:300) in blocking solution.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days, gentle shaking, protected from light)  

6 Wash  
6.1 Wash with PBST, 3 changes.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours total, protected from light)  

7 Dehydration (post-staining)  
7.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
7.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

8 Delipidation and Clearing  
8.1 Incubation with 1:2 mixture of dichloromethane (DCM) and methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
8.2 Incubation with 100% DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
8.3 Incubation with fresh 100% DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

9 Refractive Index Matching  
9.1 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) dibenzyl ether (DBE).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours, protected from light)  
9.2 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) DBE for long-term storage and imaging.(Temperature: RT, Time: ≥1 hour or until imaging)

**Chosen Method:** Ce3D  
**Chosen Labeling:** [TH + Alexa Fluor 488, CD31 + Alexa Fluor 647]  
**Justification:** The original BoneClear protocol (a solvent-based high-RI method) caused excessive brittleness in fixed mouse femurs during叔丁醇 dehydration, compromising structural integrity of the marrow cavity. Ce3D is an aqueous, non-denaturing clearing method specifically validated for hard tissues like bone and lymphoid organs, offering excellent preservation of 3D architecture with minimal shrinkage or fragility. It supports deep antibody penetration into dense mineralized tissue while preserving fluorescence of Alexa Fluor dyes. TH (tyrosine hydroxylase) is a specific marker for sympathetic nerve fibers in the bone marrow niche, and CD31 robustly labels vascular endothelial networks; both are compatible with Ce3D and can be co-detected using spectrally distinct Alexa Fluor conjugates without cross-talk. This combination enables high-fidelity 3D mapping of neuro-vascular spatial relationships across central marrow, endosteal, and metaphyseal regions.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Antibody Staining (post-fixation, pre-clearing)  
1.1 Incubation with blocking buffer (5% normal donkey serum, 0.5% Triton X-100 in PBS) to reduce non-specific binding.(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  
1.2 Incubation with primary antibodies: anti-TH (1:200) and anti-CD31 (1:100) diluted in antibody dilution buffer (1% normal donkey serum, 0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 5 days with gentle agitation)  
1.3 Washing with PBST (0.3% Triton X-100 in PBS), 3 changes.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours total, 4 hours per wash)  
1.4 Incubation with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488-conjugated anti-rabbit IgG (1:400) and Alexa Fluor 647-conjugated anti-rat IgG (1:400) in antibody dilution buffer.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 3 days with gentle agitation)  
1.5 Washing with PBST, 3 changes.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours total, 4 hours per wash)  

2 Tissue Optical Clearing  
2.1 Incubation with Ce3D-A1 solution (25% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol, 10% (wt/vol) urea, 10% (vol/vol) glycerol in PBS, pH 8.5).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.2 Incubation with Ce3D-A2 solution (50% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol, 20% (wt/vol) urea, 20% (vol/vol) glycerol in PBS, pH 8.5).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  
2.3 Incubation with Ce3D-B solution (80% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol, 30% (wt/vol) urea, 30% (vol/vol) glycerol in PBS, pH 8.5).(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  

3 Refractive Index Matching and Storage  
3.1 Incubation with Ce3D-Matching Solution (90% (wt/vol) α-thioglycerol in PBS, pH 8.5) until tissue becomes transparent and RI-matched.(Temperature: RT, Time: 12 hours)  
3.2 Transfer sample to imaging chamber filled with Ce3D-Matching Solution for light-sheet or confocal microscopy.(Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or storage at 4 ℃ for up to 2 weeks)

Tyrosine hydroxylase (TH) is a specific marker for sympathetic nerve fibers in the bone marrow, and CD31 (PECAM1) robustly labels vascular endothelial structures. Dual labeling with Alexa Fluor 488 (green) and Alexa Fluor 647 (far-red) provides spectrally separable, photostable signals compatible with FDISCO and ideal for 3D light-sheet imaging of neuro-vascular spatial relationships in the intact marrow niche.

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Phalloidin–Alexa Fluor 488, Myosin VIIa–Alexa Fluor 568, TO-PRO-3]  
**Justification:** The mouse cochlea is a dense, mineralized hard tissue embedded in the otic capsule, requiring a high-clearing-power method with deep dye penetration. FDISCO—a solvent-based, fluorescence-preserving DISCO variant—is established for hard tissues like cochlea and bone, provides strong delipidation and decalcification-like effects without harsh acid, and is compatible with Alexa Fluor dyes and nuclear counterstains. Phalloidin directly labels F-actin in stereocilia bundles without antibodies, preserving fine cytoskeletal architecture; Myosin VIIa is a well-validated, specific marker for cochlear hair cells and must be detected via immunostaining (no endogenous FP reporter assumed); TO-PRO-3 serves as a far-red nuclear counterstain compatible with FDISCO and avoids spectral overlap with the two primary signals. This combination enables simultaneous visualization of hair cell identity (Myosin VIIa), stereocilia integrity (Phalloidin), and cellular context (nuclei) across the entire spiral cochlea with minimal distortion.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Bleaching (optional but recommended for bone-associated autofluorescence)  
2.1 Incubation with chilled 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ + 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration (for immunolabeling and phalloidin staining)  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.5% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 5% (vol/vol) normal goat serum (NGS).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody and Phalloidin Staining  
5.1 Incubation with anti-Myosin VIIa primary antibody (e.g., Proteus Biosciences #25-6790, 1:200) + Phalloidin–Alexa Fluor 488 (1:100) in PBS + 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 + 5% NGS.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours with gentle agitation)  

6 Washing  
6.1 Incubation with PBS + 0.3% (vol/vol) Triton X-100.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)

**Chosen Method:** FDISCO  
**Chosen Labeling:** [Phalloidin–Alexa Fluor 647, Myosin VIIa–Alexa Fluor 488]  
**Justification:** The mouse cochlea is a dense, mineralized hard tissue embedded in the otic capsule, requiring a high-clearing-power method with deep dye/antibody penetration. FDISCO—a solvent-based, fluorescence-preserving variant of DISCO—is established for hard tissues like bone and cochlea, offering rapid, strong delipidation and refractive index (RI) matching while maintaining structural integrity of the spiral architecture. Endogenous fluorescent proteins are quenched by FDISCO solvents, so direct labeling with small-molecule probes or antibody-conjugated fluorophores is required. Phalloidin specifically labels F-actin in stereocilia bundles of both inner and outer hair cells with high contrast and minimal background, enabling precise identification of hair cell position and continuity. Myosin VIIa is a well-validated, hair cell-specific cytoplasmic marker that complements Phalloidin by labeling the entire hair cell soma, allowing unambiguous distinction between inner and outer hair cells based on morphology and spatial arrangement. Both Alexa Fluor 488 and 647 are compatible with FDISCO and provide spectrally separable signals ideal for 3D reconstruction and automated counting.

**Protocol Steps:**  
1 Dehydration  
1.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
1.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

2 Delipidation and Bleaching  
2.1 Incubation with chilled fresh 5% (vol/vol) H₂O₂ in methanol (1 volume 30% H₂O₂ to 5 volumes methanol).(Temperature: 4 ℃, Time: 12 hours)  

3 Rehydration (for immunolabeling)  
3.1 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.2 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.3 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.4 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
3.5 Incubation with PBS + 0.2% (vol/vol) Triton X-100 (PBT).(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

4 Permeabilization and Blocking  
4.1 Incubation with PBT + 10% (vol/vol) normal goat serum (NGS).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

5 Primary Antibody Staining  
5.1 Incubation with anti-Myosin VIIa primary antibody (e.g., Proteus Biosciences #25-6790, 1:200 dilution) in PBT + 5% NGS.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 48 hours)  

6 Washing  
6.1 Incubation with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
6.2 Repeat step 6.1 three times, changing solution every hour.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

7 Secondary Antibody and Phalloidin Co-staining  
7.1 Incubation with Alexa Fluor 488–conjugated secondary antibody (1:500) and Phalloidin–Alexa Fluor 647 (1:100) in PBT + 5% NGS.(Temperature: 37 ℃, Time: 24 hours)  

8 Post-staining Washes  
8.1 Incubation with PBT.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
8.2 Repeat step 8.1 two more times.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour per wash)  

9 Dehydration (pre-clearing)  
9.1 Incubation with 20% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.2 Incubation with 40% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.3 Incubation with 60% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.4 Incubation with 80% (vol/vol) methanol in PBS.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
9.5 Incubation with 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  
9.6 Incubation with fresh 100% (vol/vol) methanol.(Temperature: RT, Time: 1 hour)  

10 Clearing and Refractive Index Matching  
10.1 Incubation with dichloromethane (DCM, anhydrous, ≥99.8%).(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.2 Incubation with fresh DCM.(Temperature: RT, Time: 30 minutes)  
10.3 Incubation with benzyl alcohol:benzyl benzoate (BABB, 1:2 vol/vol).(Temperature: RT, Time: 2 hours)  

11 Imaging Preparation  
11.1 Transfer sample to glass-bottom imaging dish and submerge in BABB.(Temperature: RT, Time: immediate imaging or storage up to 1 week at 4 ℃ in dark)
